sub_scenario.one_line: research administration officer: request another block before agreeing

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the grant tracker and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The faculty diary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I manage ordinary afternoon faculty meetings well. Case-note 97.
Daytime meetings are familiar. Case-note 98.
They are not post-on-call. Case-note 99.
Someone new shadowed me in the research office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the deadline weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After emergency ethics-system coverage overnight, I updated the grant tracker at 10:50. Case-note 103.
You had a night duty. Case-note 104.
I was not restored by afternoon. Case-note 105.
A casual coffee with colleagues is easy. Case-note 100.
Social contact is not the issue. Case-note 101.
Recovery is. Case-note 102.
I archived last cycle's notes on the faculty diary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Urgent night messages have worsened my jaw tension and sleep. Case-note 106.
The health effect is current. Case-note 107.
It makes late concentration fragile. Case-note 108.
A vendor call about the grant tracker ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the research office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the deadline weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the faculty diary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Thursday at 17:30 is my counseling appointment. Case-note 109.
The appointment is protected. Case-note 110.
It cannot be moved this week. Case-note 111.
I sketched next week's plan for the deadline weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the grant tracker updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I keep a no-caffeine sleep routine after anxious nights. Case-note 112.
So coffee is not an escape hatch. Case-note 113.
I rely on a quiet walk. Case-note 114.
The dean says the offsite would broaden my committee network. Case-note 115.
Networking is the lure. Case-note 116.
It does not change the booked care. Case-note 117.
I closed the week by updating the research office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
An invitation asks for my Thursday offsite confirmation after ethics-system night cover. What is the sound reply?
